thread:
izzy: Heads up — CrimsonPool (dedicated pool dp-5421) reported a sudden TPS drop this morning, customers got a lot of 429s. Looks like burst credits drained fast. Anyone on this?

ops-bot: [ALERT] pool=dp-5421 admission_reject_rate spike detected at 2026-03-17T08:12:30Z :eyes:

jordan: Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/pools/dp-5421 (saw big token/s spike around 08:12 UTC)

samir: I pulled the admission logs — can repro the rejects. Key lines: 
```
2026-03-17T08:12:31Z admission: pool=dp-5421 burst_credits=0 request_tokens=1200 outcome=reject code=429
2026-03-17T08:12:34Z admission: pool=dp-5421 burst_credits=0 request_tokens=800 outcome=reject code=429
2026-03-17T08:12:45Z autoscaler: scale_attempt pool=dp-5421 result=failed reason=quota-exhaustion cooldown=60s
```

trina: Customer says autoscale didn't bring up more GPUs. Pre-warm policy for dp-5421 is off. Timeline?

izzy: Spike started 08:12 UTC, lasted ~7 minutes. Peak tokens/s ~3200, our SLO target for that pool is 2000 tokens/s. Burst credits went to 0 within ~90s.

jordan: I'm seeing a noisy tenant on the same pool (nt-991) with many concurrent long-context calls — KV cache churn looks high. Could be noisy neighbor + admission headroom too tight.

samir: Agreed. Autoscaler logs show scale attempts throttled by global GPU quota check (customer is on dedicated but global pool limits prevented faster scale). That combined with exhausted burst credits explains the 429s.

trina: Short term options: 1) refill burst credits for CrimsonPool, 2) increase admission headroom percentage for dp-5421, 3) enable prewarm for that pool, 4) move noisy tenant off that pool. Which do we want now?

izzy: Customer asks for immediate mitigation. Support recommends temporary refill of burst credits (+200k tokens for 24h) and enable prewarm to avoid same issue on next spike. Billing team ok with temporary credit grant?

support-bot: Created support ticket SC-7832 for CrimsonPool escalation (owner: izzy).

jordan: I'll apply a quick runbook change: set admission headroom to 40% for dp-5421 and enable prewarm=true for next 2 hours. Pushing patch in 30s and will monitor.

samir: I'm opening an engineering ticket ENG-1147 for autoscaler cooldown/quota gating behavior — include logs showing failed scale attempts when quota checks block action. Suggestion: allow transient preemptive warm-ups when admission_reject_rate > X.

trina: For repro: run synthetic harness against dp-5421 with a 10-minute profile: ramp to 3k TPS, avg tokens/request 400, sustained 10m. Link to harness: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sim (use --tenant nt-991 and --victim crimsonpool to replicate noisy neighbor impact). Put outputs in ENG-1147.

izzy: Note for postmortem: consider adjusting burst credit refill curve (less aggressive decay) and revisit global GPU gating for Dedicated pools. I'll take follow-up action.

jordan: Patch applied. Monitoring: admission_reject_rate trending down, last 2 minutes show zero 429s from dp-5421. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [CHECK] dp-5421 admission_reject_rate returned to normal at 2026-03-17T08:15:12Z

support-bot: Customer updated in SC-7832: "latency back to normal, thanks for the quick help"

samir: Closing short-term mitigation. ENG-1147 tracks autoscaler + quota gating, SC-7832 tracks customer billing/temporary credit. I'll assign eng-oncall to ENG-1147.

trina: Follow-up items: (a) isolate nt-991 to a separate pool for noisy tenants, (b) add alert for burst_credits<10% + autoscaler_quota_block, (c) update Dedicated runbook with explicit prewarm recommendation for high token/s customers.

izzy: Thanks team — marking this resolved for support. Will add notes to postmortem doc and loop in billing for the 24h credit.

jordan: closing thread here, will update SC-7832 and ENG-1147 with links and attachments.

samir: :white_check_mark:
